text:
aj: Seeing repeated gRPC streaming stalls on batch-infer pods in us-west-2. Tail latency spikes and streams just hang for ~30s then resume. Noticed packet retransmits in app logs.

maria: :eyes: any recent network changes or kernel/driver updates on that fleet?

noah: Yesterday we rolled calico 3.21 -> 3.22 on a subset. Also bumped node image (linux-5.15 -> 5.19) on the same ASG.

aj: Good catch. I reproduced locally between two pods on the same nodepair using a simple gRPC stream — `kubectl exec` + small client — and saw identical stalls.

maria: Can you paste `ip link` and `ethtool -k` from both nodes? suspecting GSO/GRO interaction with MTU/clamping.

aj: Here — pasted from node-a: ```
2: eth0: mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 0a:1b:2c:3d:4e:5f brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
    GSO: on  GRO: on  LRO: off
```

aj: node-b had ENI configured with MTU 9000 at the infra layer but the pod veths were 1500. tracepath to pod IP shows a hop drop at 1500 -> 1380.

infra-bot: [alert] packet-loss-percent(us-west-2-e2e) = 3.4% over last 10m.

sophia: That smells like path MTU shadowing / egress clamp — something on the host or transit is dropping DF=1 fragments causing gRPC streaming with large frames to stall while TCP tries to retransmit. RDMA nodes also show partial reassembly failures reported in dmesg on a couple of hosts.

noah: We also enabled Geneve encap fixes for calico which added 50 bytes overhead yesterday. If the veths stayed at 1500 but underlying overlay path expects 1450, fragments will be created and if intermediate drops DF packets you get stalls.

maria: Quick mitigation: lower pod MTU to 1400 via CHAIN/daemonset or set host-level iptables rule to clear DF bit for fragments (NOT ideal). Long term: align MTU end-to-end (set pod veth and host interfaces to 9000 or negotiate) and ensure GSO offload adjustments for overlay.

aj: Trying a fast mitigation: patched a node to `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` and reduced calico veth to 1400 on a canary. Re-tested gRPC stream and stalls disappeared on that pair.

oncall-ops: Can we roll this as a targeted canary to remaining us-west-2 GPU nodes? Need plan: change pod MTU in CNI config -> drain -> reboot? or use live update? Also check RDMA NICs (Mellanox) where jumbo frames are preferred.

maria: Plan suggestion: 1) Bake calico CNI config with pod mtu 1400 and enable `mtu_probing=1` cluster-wide flag; 2) Drain nodes in ASG batches, verify no regressions; 3) For RDMA/GPU nodes where performance requires 9000, coordinate with cloud-networking to ensure all intermediate hops allow jumbo + adjust geneve/encap sizes. 4) Add monitoring to alert on DF drops and reassembly failures.

aj: Agree. I'll open a rollout doc + runbook and start a 10-node canary in the affected ASG. For now mark this as P2 but with high operational risk. :thumbsup:

sophia: Also adding a temporary app-level fallback: smaller chunk sizes for streams to avoid large single-frame sends until MTU is fixed.

aj: Thanks all — posting notes in incident board and will ping when canary results in 1h.
